domain: Public Health Policy / Medical Ethics / Constitutional Law
topic_summary: Analysis of vaccine mandates as a contested kernel where different readings of the legitimacy-of-coercion commitment produce structurally distinct constraints with non-overlapping victim sets. The public-health-primary reading treats unvaccinated individuals as vectors requiring containment; the bodily-autonomy-primary reading treats mandate enforcement as impermissible state coercion regardless of collective benefit.

key_entities: Immunocompromised populations (vulnerable to infection when vaccination rates drop)
Vaccine-hesitant individuals (subject to coercion under mandate regimes)
Public health authorities (claim police power to mandate based on Jacobson precedent)
Healthcare workers (required vaccination pre-COVID; contested during COVID)
State legislatures (California SB277 eliminated exemptions post-measles outbreak)
Supreme Court (Jacobson v. Massachusetts 1904 established police power doctrine)
key_tensions: Individual bodily autonomy vs collective disease prevention (mandate opponents vs public health advocates)
Consent rights of vaccine recipients vs consent rights of those exposed to unvaccinated (competing victim sets)
Trust preservation vs immediate coverage gains (mandate backlash risk vs utilitarian benefit)
key_mechanisms: Herd immunity threshold enforcement (mandates raise vaccination rates above transmission-blocking threshold)
School entry requirements (all 50 states use education access as leverage for compliance)
Healthcare worker employment conditions (vaccination as condition of patient contact)
Exemption elimination (California SB277 removed personal/religious exemptions after outbreak)
key_absences: Differential mandate justification by disease severity (measles vs flu vs COVID treated equivalently in debate despite different R0 and mortality)
Exit option analysis (whether unvaccinated can meaningfully exit shared spaces vs captive populations like schools)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The legitimacy of state coercion to compel medical intervention for collective benefit
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Jacobson precedent grants states police power to mandate vaccination; authority grounded in utilitarian harm-prevention rather than consent

readings.commitment: State may compel medical intervention when collective harm-prevention outweighs individual autonomy
readings.authority_grounding: Jacobson precedent; utilitarian calculus; police power doctrine
readings.expected_structural_delta: Unvaccinated individuals enter victim set as coerced subjects; immunocompromised exit victim set as protected beneficiaries; high ε from enforcement apparatus

readings.commitment: Medical intervention without consent is categorically impermissible regardless of collective benefit
readings.authority_grounding: Deontological consent rights; Nuremberg Code; bodily integrity as non-negotiable
readings.expected_structural_delta: Immunocompromised individuals enter victim set as exposed to unvaccinated; mandate enforcers enter beneficiary set; moderate ε from non-enforcement

readings.commitment: Coercion legitimacy scales with disease severity and transmission dynamics; measles justifies mandates, flu does not
readings.authority_grounding: Harm principle; least-restrictive-means doctrine; R0 and mortality thresholds
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set varies by pathogen; high-R0/high-mortality diseases trigger coercion; low-severity diseases do not; moderate ε from case-by-case adjudication

axiom_contradictions.basis: Public-health-primary accepts utilitarian override of consent when collective benefit suffices; bodily-autonomy-primary treats consent as non-overridable regardless of collective benefit. No single framework holds both: accepting utilitarian override as legitimate requires rejecting consent as absolute, and vice versa.

omegas.description: At what R0/CFR threshold does proportionality_reading collapse into public_health_primary? If no threshold exists, proportionality is a rhetorical compromise rather than a structural reading.

Does exit-option availability change coercion legitimacy? School mandates apply to captive populations (children cannot exit education); workplace mandates apply to adults with employment mobility. If exit matters, bodily_autonomy_primary may be a piton of voluntary-association norms rather than a universal principle.
omegas.source: Deferred axis exit_option_asymmetry; Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Are immunocompromised individuals passive victims or active claimants? If they demand mandate enforcement, victim/beneficiary classification inverts. Research context treats them as vulnerable populations; unclear if they claim coercion-rights over others.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan); entity extraction ambiguity

omegas.description: Is Jacobson precedent a mountain (constitutional bedrock) or a rope (contingent judicial interpretation)? Post-Dobbs jurisprudence may reclassify bodily-autonomy constraints, destabilizing public_health_primary authority grounding.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: Jacobson precedent treated as stable authority grounding for public_health_primary reading, but post-Dobbs constitutional jurisprudence on bodily autonomy may reclassify this as contingent rope rather than mountain. Generated omega_jacobson_precedent_stability to bound this uncertainty. No tunnel vision: readings derived from deontological ethics, utilitarian ethics, and harm-principle jurisprudence (three distinct lenses). No epistemic trespass: domain is public health policy and constitutional law, well within training data coverage.
